title: Yemen’s Houthis capture Red Sea port of Mocha
gist: An Al-Monitor Middle East Minute episode reports Yemen's Houthis capturing the Red Sea port of Mocha, Algeria severing relations with the UAE, and a new poll showing Palestinians losing trust in both Hamas and Fatah.

insights.claim: Yemen's Houthis have captured the Red Sea port of Mocha, extending their control of Yemen's western coastline and its port infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Control of a Red Sea port gives the Houthis logistics and interdiction depth near Bab al-Mandeb, a structural negative for Suez-routed shipping economics.
insights.locator: Yemen's Houthis capture Red Sea port of Mocha

insights.claim: Algeria has severed relations with the United Arab Emirates, a formal diplomatic break between two significant Arab states.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A North Africa-Gulf diplomatic rupture signals deepening intra-Arab fragmentation that can complicate Emirati investment and logistics positions in the Maghreb.
insights.locator: Algeria severed relations with the UAE

insights.claim: A new poll shows Palestinians are losing trust in both Hamas and Fatah, meaning the credibility loss is system-wide rather than favoring one faction.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Simultaneous delegitimization of both main factions undercuts any day-after governance plan that relies on either one, raising execution risk for reconstruction schemes.
insights.locator: a new poll showed Palestinians are losing trust in both Hamas and Fatah
